body.text: Cīvaravastu
body.translated_text: The Section on Robes (<s>Cīvaravastu</s>)

children.translated_text: MSV II 3
) In the Section on Robes, the summary verse:

children.text: jīvako bhāṅgakaś caiva tathā dīrghadaśāni ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Jīvaka</s>, and <s>Bhāṅgaka</s>, and likewise the long edges,
the rains-cut should be known,
the death, <s>Upananda</s>, the sick one is the last.

body.text: piṇḍoddānam* /
body.translated_text: Summary verse:

children.translated_text: <s>Jīvaka</s>, three cut ones, rain-garment, sitting-cloth,
itch, <s>Sugata</s>, silk, wool, hemp, and linen.

body.text: uddānam* /
body.translated_text: Summary verse:

children.text: khaṇḍo gopaś ca siṃhaś ca vaiśālīgamanaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Khaṇḍa</s>, <s>Gopa</s>, and <s>Siṃha</s>, and the journey to <s>Vaiśālī</s>,
<s>Celā</s>, the anger of the seer, and with <s>Āmrapālī</s>'s fear.
The merchant's wife, the birth of <s>Jīvaka</s>, and the tradition of medicine,
<s>Takṣaśilā</s>, <s>Bhadraṅkara</s>, <s>Udumbara</s>, <s>Kārṣamāpaka</s>.
<s>Rohitaka</s>, the royal garden, <s>Mathurā</s>, the <s>Malla</s> women,

children.text: yamunā śivapathikā vaiśālyām akṣi śatapadī sapta /
children.translated_text: <s>Yamunā</s>, <s>Śivapathikā</s>, in <s>Vaiśālī</s> the eye, the centipede, seven,
in <s>Rājagṛha</s> five matters—thus the section on <s>Jīvaka</s> is summarized.

body.text: videheṣu videharājo (

children.text: ) rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ cākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca / tasya khaṇḍapramukhāni paṃcāmātyaśatāni / khaṇḍo 'grāmātyo dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayati nyāyataś ca vyavahārān paśyati yataḥ sarva eva janakāyas tanmukho 'vasthitaḥ / tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* / sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati (
children.translated_text: ) was ruling the kingdom, and it was prosperous and thriving and secure and well-provisioned and teeming with many people. He had five hundred ministers headed by <s>Khaṇḍa</s>. <s>Khaṇḍa</s>, the chief minister, governed the kingdom righteously and adjudicated disputes justly, so that all the populace stood looking to him. He had brought a wife from a family equal to his own. He played with her, (
MSV II 4

children.text: ) ramate paricārayati / tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putro jātaḥ / tasya trīṇi saptakāny ekaviṃśati divasān pūrvavad yāvad gopa iti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam* / bhūyo 'py asya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putro jātaḥ / tasyāpi pūrvavad vistareṇa siṃha iti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam* / gopaḥ siṃhaś ca kramaśas taruṇau saṃvṛttau / khaṇḍo 'grāmātyaḥ pūrvam eva śūro vikrāntaḥ pañcasu sthāneṣu kṛtāvi yenāmātyānām agraḥ / yadā putrabalī jātas tadā bhūyasyā mātrayā sarvāmātyān abhibhūyāvasthitaḥ / tatas te 'mātyā upahatatejasaḥ parasparaṃ saṃjalpaṃ kṛtvā saṃjātāmarṣā rājñaḥ sakāśaṃ gatāḥ / tato 'vasaraṃ jñātvā rājānam ūcuḥ / deva ko rājā / rājā kathayati / kuto bhavatāṃ vimarṣo 'haṃ rājā ko 'nya iti / te kathayanti / deva khaṇḍo rājā na devaḥ / yadi tasyābhirucitaṃ syād devaṃ rājyāc cyāvayitvā svayam eva paṭṭaṃ baddhā rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kārayed iti / rājā saṃlakṣayati / sarva ete tenābhibhūtās tena bhedaṃ kurvantīti / yāvad apareṇa samayena rājā amātyagaṇaparivṛtas tiṣṭhati / khaṇḍaś cāgrāmātyo 'rthipratyarthiśatasahasraparivṛto rājakulaṃ praviṣṭaḥ / pūrṇaṃ tad rājakulam avasthitam* / yadā tu rājakṛtiṃ kṛtvā niṣkrāntas tadā tad rājakulaṃ śūnyam avasthitam* / rājā kathayati / bhavantaḥ sarva evāyaṃ janakāyo niṣkrāmati / amātyair avatāro labdhaḥ / te kathayanti / sākṣātkṛtaṃ devena yato vijñāpayāmaḥ / yadi (
children.translated_text: ) enjoyed himself, and attended to her. While he was playing, enjoying, and attending to her, a son was born to him. For that son, for three weeks—twenty-one days—as before, in full detail, the name <s>Gopa</s> was established. Again, while he was playing, enjoying, and attending, another son was born. For that one too, as before, in full detail, the name <s>Siṃha</s> was established. <s>Gopa</s> and <s>Siṃha</s> gradually grew up. <s>Khaṇḍa</s>, the chief minister, had already been brave and valiant, accomplished in the five arts, and therefore foremost among the ministers. When his sons grew strong, he all the more overwhelmed all the other ministers. Then those ministers, their power diminished, having consulted among themselves and become indignant, went to the king. Then, finding an opportune moment, they said to the king: 'Lord, who is king?' The king said: 'What is your doubt? I am the king—who else?' They said: 'Lord, <s>Khaṇḍa</s> is the king, not Your Majesty. If he wished, he could depose Your Majesty from the kingdom, bind the royal turban on his own head, and exercise sovereign power.' The king considered: 'All these have been overwhelmed by him; therefore they are creating discord.' After some time, the king was seated surrounded by the assembly of ministers. <s>Khaṇḍa</s>, the chief minister, entered the royal court surrounded by hundreds of thousands of petitioners and respondents. The royal court was full. But when he had conducted the royal business and departed, the royal court stood empty. The king said: 'Gentlemen, all the people leave with him.' The ministers seized the opportunity. They said: 'Your Majesty has seen it with his own eyes—this is what we were informing you about. If (
MSV II 5

children.text: ) khaṇḍasyābhirucitaṃ syād eva rājyāc cyāvayitvā svayam eva paṭṭaṃ baddhā rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kārayed iti / kākaśaṅkino hi rājānaḥ / sa saṃlakṣayati / yathaite kathayanti nūnam evam iti / sa tasyāvatāraprekṣī saṃvṛttaḥ / mitrāmitramadhyamā lokāḥ / yāvad aparaiḥ khaṇḍasyārocitam* / rājā tavāvatāraprekṣy avatiṣṭhate / kṣamaṃ manyasveti / tasya śaṃkā samutpannā / sa vicārayituṃ pravṛttaḥ / kva gacchāmīti / yadi śrāvastīṃ gāmiṣyāmi rājādhīnā śrāvastī tatrāpy eṣa evādīnavaḥ / evaṃ vārāṇasyāṃ rājagṛhe caṇpāyām ekādhīnatvād eṣa evādīnavaḥ / vaiśālī gaṇādhīnā / yadṛśānām abhipretaṃ tad viṃśatīnāṃ nābhipretam* / sarvathā vaiśālīṃ gacchāmīti / tena vaiśālakānāṃ licchavīnāṃ dūtasaṃpreṣaṇaṃ kṛtam* / gacchāmy ahaṃ bhavatāṃ bāhucchāyāyāṃ vastum iti / tair ādarajātaiḥ pratisandeśo dattaḥ / iyam eva vaiśālī svāgatam āgaccheti / tataḥ khaṇḍenāgrāmātyena jñātaya āhūya uktāḥ / bhavanto vaiśālīṃ saṃprasthito yeṣāṃ yuṣmākam abhirucitam ihāvasthānaṃ te (
children.translated_text: ) <s>Khaṇḍa</s> wished, he could depose Your Majesty from the kingdom, bind the royal turban on his own head, and exercise sovereign power.' For kings are suspicious even of crows. He considered: 'As they say, so it must be.' He began watching for an opportunity against him. People in the world are friends, enemies, or neutral. After some time, others informed <s>Khaṇḍa</s>: 'The king is watching for an opportunity against you; consider what is best.' Suspicion arose in him. He began to deliberate: 'Where shall I go? If I go to <s>Śrāvastī</s>—<s>Śrāvastī</s> is under a king's authority; the same danger exists there. Likewise in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in <s>Campā</s>—being under one ruler, the same danger exists. <s>Vaiśālī</s> is governed by a council. What is desired by some is not desired by the twenty. In any case, I shall go to <s>Vaiśālī</s>.' He sent a message to the <s>Licchavi</s> people of <s>Vaiśālī</s>: 'I am going to dwell in the shade of your arms.' Those, being honored, sent a reply: 'This is <s>Vaiśālī</s> itself—welcome, come!' Then <s>Khaṇḍa</s>, the chief minister, having summoned his kinsmen, said: 'Gentlemen, I am setting out for <s>Vaiśālī</s>. Those of you who wish to stay here, (

children.text: ) 'bhitiṣṭhantu yeṣāṃ nābhirucitaṃ te sajjā bhavantu gacchāmaḥ / gopālakāḥ paśupālakāś coktāḥ / yūyaṃ gomahiṣīḥ yena vaiśālīṃ tena khaṭayata / pauruṣeyā uktāḥ / sannāhayata vaiśālīṃ gacchāma iti / tato janakāyam evaṃ prerayitvā rājñaḥ sakāśaṃ gataḥ pādayor nipatya kathayati / deva kiṃcit karaṇīyam asti / udyānaṃ gacchāmy (
children.translated_text: ) let them stay; those who do not wish to, let them get ready—we are going.' The cowherds and cattle-keepers were told: 'You—drive the cows and buffaloes toward <s>Vaiśālī</s>.' The servants were told: 'Make ready—we are going to <s>Vaiśālī</s>.' Then, having set the populace in motion thus, he went to the king, fell at his feet, and said: 'Lord, there is something I must do. I am going to the park— (
MSV II 6

children.text: ) avalokito bhaveti / rājā kathayaty evaṃ bhavatu gaccheti / sodyānaśobhāṃ kārayitvā sārādānaṃ śakaṭeṣv āropya upari khādanīyabhojanīyena ācchādya saṃprasthitaḥ / amātyaiḥ śrutam* / khaṇḍo niṣpalāyatīti / te tvaritaṃ tvaritaṃ rājñaḥ sakāśaṃ gatvā kathayanti / deva khaṇḍo niṣpalāyatīti / rājā kathayati / bhavanto gacchata nirvartayateti / te caturaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ sannāhya nirgatāḥ kathayanti / khaṇḍa devo śabdayatīti nivartayasveti / sa kathayati / bhavanto yuṣmākaṃ dīrgharātram ayam āśvāsakaḥ / aho bata khaṇḍaḥ kālaṃ kuryān niṣpalāyeta iti vā iti / sa yuṣmākam alpakṛcchreṇa paripūrṇaḥ / gacchata niṣpalāyaty ayam iti / te rājñaś cittānurakṣayā kāṇḍakāṇḍiṃ kṛtvā nivṛttā rājñaḥ kathayanti / deva niṣpalāyitaḥ khaṇḍo agrāmātya iti / rājā kathayati / na śobhanam iti kṛtvā tūṣṇīm avasthitaḥ / khaṇḍo 'py anupūrveṇa vaiśālīṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: ) please look after things.' The king said: 'Very well, go.' Having had the garden decorated, he loaded the goods onto carts, covered them on top with food and provisions, and set out. The ministers heard: '<s>Khaṇḍa</s> is fleeing!' They hurriedly went to the king and said: 'Lord, <s>Khaṇḍa</s> is fleeing!' The king said: 'Gentlemen, go and deal with it.' They, having equipped a four-division army, went out and said: '<s>Khaṇḍa</s>, the lord commands you to turn back.' He replied: 'Gentlemen, for a long time you have had this consolation: "Oh, if only <s>Khaṇḍa</s> would die or flee!" That wish of yours has been fulfilled with little trouble. Go—this one is fleeing.' They, out of regard for the king's feelings, fought a skirmish and returned, telling the king: 'Lord, <s>Khaṇḍa</s> the chief minister has fled.' The king said: 'This is not good,' and remained silent. <s>Khaṇḍa</s> proceeded by stages to <s>Vaiśālī</s>.

body.translated_text: Among the <s>Videhas</s>, the <s>Videha</s> king (

body.text: tena khalu samayena vaiśālī tribhiḥ skandhaiḥ prativasati / prathame skandhe sapta kūṭāgārasahasrāṇi suvarṇamayair niryūhair madhyame skandhe caturdaśa rūpyamayair niryūhair adharime skandhe ekaviṃśatis tāmramayair niryūhais teṣu yathāyogaṃ manuṣyāḥ pratvasanti / uttamā madhyamā adhamā / vaiśālyāṃ gaṇena kriyākārā vyavasthāpitāḥ / yā prathame (

children.translated_text: MSV II 7

children.text: ) skandhe dārikā jāyate sā prathama eva skandhe dīyate na madhyame nādharime / yā madhyame sā prathame skandhe dīyate madhyame vā nādharime / yādharime sā triṣv api skandheṣu dīyate / kanyāyā anirvāhaḥ nānyatra dīyate iti / vaiśālīstrīratnaṃ na kasyacid dīyate / gaṇasāmānyaṃ paribhojyam eva / khaṇḍasya pradhānapuruṣa iti kṛtvā prathame skandhe gṛhaṃ dattam* / tatra prativastum ārabdhaḥ /
children.translated_text: ) section was given only in the first section, not in the middle or lower. A girl from the middle section was given in the first or middle section, not in the lower. A girl from the lower section was given in all three sections. An unmarried girl was not given elsewhere. The jewel among <s>Vaiśālī</s>'s women was not given to anyone—she was common property of the council, to be enjoyed by all. <s>Khaṇḍa</s>, being considered a man of importance, was given a house in the first section. He began to reside there.

body.translated_text: Now at that time, <s>Vaiśālī</s> was inhabited in three sections. In the first section there were seven thousand multi-storied mansions with golden finials; in the middle section fourteen [thousand] with silver finials; in the lowest section twenty-one [thousand] with copper finials. In these, people dwelt according to their rank—superior, middling, and inferior. In <s>Vaiśālī</s>, regulations were established by the council. A girl born in the first (

body.text: yadā gaṇaḥ saṃnipatati tadāsāv āhūyamāno 'pi na saṃnipatati / sa vaiśālakair ucyate / khaṇḍa kasmāt tvaṃ na saṃnipatasīti / sa kathayati / saṃnipatitād eva ayam ādīnavaḥ prādurbhūto nāhaṃ saṃnipatāmīti / vaiśālakāḥ kathayanti / khaṇḍa saṃnipāte ko 'tra ādīnavo bhaviṣyatīti / sa saṃnipatitum ārabdhaḥ / mataṃ nānuprayacchati / te kathayanti / khaṇḍa matam anuprayaccheti / sa kathayati / matam api nānuprayacchāmi yasmān matād eva me ādīnavāḥ prādurbhūtā iti / te kathayanti / anuprayaccha matam* / ko 'trādīnavo bhaviṣyatīti / sa ca nigame saṃnipatati mataṃ cānuprayacchati / pūrvaṃ vaiśālakā licchavayo yasya kasyacil lekham anupreṣayanti sakarkaśam anupreṣayanti / yadā tu khaṇḍo mataṃ dātum ārabdhas tadā sānunayaṃ likhanti / (

children.translated_text: MSV II 8
) Those to whom (

children.text: ) lekho nīto bhavati / te parasparaṃ saṃjalpaṃ kurvanti / bhavantaḥ ko yogo yena vaiśālako gaṇaḥ pūrvaṃ sakarkaśaṃ likhati idānīṃ tu sānunayam iti / apare kathayanti / asti viśeṣaḥ / videharājasya khaṇḍo nāmāgrāmātya ihāgatas tasya matenānuvyavaharanti yenādhunā sānunayaṃ likhantīti /
children.translated_text: ) the courteous letter was brought—they talked among themselves: 'Gentlemen, what has happened that the <s>Vaiśālī</s> council, which previously wrote harshly, now writes courteously?' Others said: 'There is a reason. The chief minister of the <s>Videha</s> king, named <s>Khaṇḍa</s>, has come here; they conduct business according to his opinion, which is why they now write courteously.'

body.translated_text: When the council assembled, he, though summoned, would not attend. The <s>Vaiśālī</s> people said to him: '<s>Khaṇḍa</s>, why do you not attend the assembly?' He replied: 'It was from attending assemblies that this calamity befell me; I will not attend.' The <s>Vaiśālī</s> people said: '<s>Khaṇḍa</s>, what calamity could there be in the assembly?' He began to attend. But he would not give his opinion. They said: '<s>Khaṇḍa</s>, give your opinion.' He replied: 'I will not give my opinion either, for it was from giving opinions that calamities befell me.' They said: 'Give your opinion—what calamity could there be?' So he attended the council and gave his opinion. Previously, when the <s>Licchavi</s> people of <s>Vaiśālī</s> sent letters to anyone, they sent them harshly. But when <s>Khaṇḍa</s> began giving his opinion, they wrote courteously. (

body.text: khaṇḍena gopasya siṃhasya ca niveśanaṃ kṛtam* / siṃhasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayato duhitā jātā / tasyāpi vistareṇa jātimahaṃ kṛtvā celeti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam* / sā naimittikena dṛṣṭvā vyākṛtā putraṃ janayiṣyati / sa pitaraṃ jīvitād vyaparopya svayam eva paṭṭaṃ baddhvā rājyaṃ kārayiṣyatīti / bhūyo 'sya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayato duhitā jātā / tasya api vistareṇa jātimahaṃ kṛtvopaceleti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam* / sāpi naimittikena vyākṛtā putraṃ janayiṣyati lakṣaṇasaṃpūrṇam iti / gopo vyāḍo vikrānto vaiśālakānāṃ licchavīnām udyānāni vināśayati / udyānapālair ucyate / vaiśālakā licchavayo vyāḍā vikrāntāḥ / mā teṣām udyānāni vināśayeti / sa nivāryamāṇo 'pi na saṃtiṣṭhate / udyānapālaiḥ khaṇḍasyārocitam* / putras te vaiśālakānāṃ licchavīnām udyānāni vināśayati / nivārayainam* / licchavayo vyāḍā vikrāntā māsyānarthaṃ kariṣyanti / sa tenāhūyoktaḥ / putra vaiśālakā licchavayo vyāḍā vikrāntā mā teṣām udyānāni vināśaya mā te anarthaṃ kariṣyantīti / sa kathayati / tāta eṣām udyānāni santi asmākaṃ tu na santi / sa kathayti / putra udyānasyārthāya gaṇaṃ (

children.translated_text: MSV II 9

children.text: ) vijñāpayāmīti / tena gaṇo vijñapto mama putrayor udyānaṃ nāsti /tad arhaṃ mama udyāne prasādaṃ kartum iti / tais tābhyāṃ jīrṇodyānaṃ dattam* / tasmin mahāśālavṛkṣaḥ / tatraikena bhagavataḥ pratimā kāritā / dvitīyena vihāraḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ / tathā sthavirair api sūtrānte upanibaddhaṃ buddho bhagavān vaiśālyāṃ viharati gopasiṃhaśālavane iti / gopaḥ akriyāsahasrāṇi karoti / licchavayo 'vadhyāyanti kṣipanti vivācayanti / tataḥ khaṇḍenāhūyoktaḥ / putra gaccha tvam amuka karvaṭaṃ tatra svādhiṣṭhitān karmāntān kāraya / tiṣṭha mā gaṇaprakopo bhaviṣyatīti / sa tatra gatvā svādhiṣṭhitān karmāntān kārayitum ārabdhaḥ / yāvad apareṇa samayena vaiśālyāṃ senāpatiḥ kālagataḥ / taiḥ khaṇḍo 'grāmātyaḥ senāpatye sthāpitaḥ / so 'pi kaṃcit kālaṃ dharmeṇa senāpatyaṃ kārayitvā kālagataḥ / vaiśālako gaṇaḥ saṃnipatitaḥ / kaṃ senāpatiṃ sthāpayāma iti / tatra eke kathayanti / khaṇḍenāgrāmātyena gaṇaḥ paripālitaḥ / tasyaiva putraṃ sthāpayāma iti / apare kathayanti / tasya putro gopo vyāḍo vikrāntaḥ / yady asau senāpatye sthāpyate niyataṃ gaṇasya bhedaṃ kariṣyati yas tu tasya bhrātā siṃhaḥ sa sūrataḥ (
children.translated_text: ) pleasant to live with, and able to win the council's affection. If the council approves, let us appoint him as commander.' All approved. They went together to <s>Siṃha</s>: '<s>Siṃha</s>, accept the commandership.' He replied: 'My (

children.text: ) sukhasaṃvāsaḥ śaknoti gaṇasya cittam ārāgayitum* / yadi gaṇasyābhirucitaṃ taṃ senāpatiṃ sthāpayāma iti / sarveṣām abhirucitam* / te saṃbhūya siṃhasya sakāśaṃ gatāḥ / siṃha senāpatitvaṃ pratīccheti / sa kathayati / mama (

children.translated_text: The elder brother <s>Gopa</s> [said]: 'Make him the general.' They said: '<s>Siṃha</s>, the generalship does not come by hereditary succession in your family. Whoever is approved by the assembly becomes general. If you are not agreeable, we shall appoint another general.' He reflected: 'If the generalship passes away from our house to another, that is not proper. I shall accept it in any case.' He made this resolution. He was installed as general by them with great honor. The <s>Vaiśālikas</s> (people of Vaiśālī) formerly used to send their letters [beginning]: 'The assembly headed by <s>Khaṇḍa</s> commands.' When <s>Siṃha</s> became general, [they wrote]: 'The assembly headed by <s>Siṃha</s> commands.' Then, at another time, a letter arrived at the town where <s>Gopa</s> was supervising his estates. <s>Gopa</s> opened and had it read. He said: 'Sirs, formerly the <s>Vaiśālika</s> assembly would write "The assembly headed by <s>Khaṇḍa</s> commands." Now they write "The assembly headed by <s>Siṃha</s> commands." Has our father died?' They said: 'He has died.' Filled with resentment, he went to <s>Vaiśālī</s> and said: 'Brother, is it proper for you to assume the generalship while I, the elder, am still alive?' <s>Siṃha</s> informed him of the events as they had occurred. He, filled with resentment toward the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vaiśālikas</s>, reflected: 'I have been treated with disrespect by the <s>Vaiśālikas</s>. I shall go to <s>Rājagṛha</s>.' He sent a messenger to King <s>Bimbisāra</s>: 'I wish to dwell under the protection of Your Majesty.' [The king] wrote back to him: 'Welcome! Come.' He went to <s>Rājagṛha</s>. body.translated_text: <s>Khaṇḍa</s> arranged marriages for <s>Gopa</s> and <s>Siṃha</s>. While <s>Siṃha</s> was playing, enjoying, and attending to his wife, a daughter was born. For her too, in full detail, having performed the birth celebration, the name <s>Celā</s> was established. She was examined by a soothsayer and pronounced: 'She will bear a son. He will kill his father and, binding the royal turban on his own head, will rule the kingdom.' Again, while he was playing, enjoying, and attending, another daughter was born. For her too, in full detail, having performed the birth celebration, the name <s>Upacelā</s> was established. She too was pronounced by a soothsayer: 'She will bear a son endowed with all the marks.' <s>Gopa</s>, who was rough and bold, destroyed the parks of the <s>Licchavi</s> people of <s>Vaiśālī</s>. The park-keepers told him: 'The <s>Licchavi</s> people of <s>Vaiśālī</s> are fierce and bold; do not destroy their parks.' But though restrained, he did not stop. The park-keepers informed <s>Khaṇḍa</s>: 'Your son is destroying the parks of the <s>Licchavi</s> people of <s>Vaiśālī</s>. Restrain him. The <s>Licchavis</s> are fierce and bold—they will cause him harm.' He summoned his son and said: 'Son, the <s>Licchavi</s> people of <s>Vaiśālī</s> are fierce and bold; do not destroy their parks, lest they cause you harm.' He replied: 'Father, they have parks but we do not.' He said: 'Son, I will petition the council for a park.' He petitioned the council: 'My sons have no park. May you be pleased to grant a park.' They gave them an old park. In it was a great <s>śāla</s> tree. There one of them had an image of the Blessed One made, and the other established a monastery. Thus the elders too have recorded in a <s>sūtra</s>: 'The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, was dwelling in <s>Vaiśālī</s> in the <s>Gopa</s>-<s>Siṃha</s> <s>Śāla</s> grove.' <s>Gopa</s> committed a thousand offenses. The <s>Licchavis</s> censured, reproached, and abused him. Then <s>Khaṇḍa</s> summoned him and said: 'Son, go to such-and-such a township; there, oversee the works properly. Stay there—lest the council become angered.' He went there and began to oversee the works properly. After some time, the military commander of <s>Vaiśālī</s> died. He posted guard-men all around the garden and began counting the days. On the seventh day, in that garden—cleared of stones, gravel, and pebbles, sprinkled with sandalwood water, bound with fragrant incense-bells, draped with silk ribbons, strewn with flowers, resounding with various songs and music—surrounded by friends, relatives, and kinfolk, he went out with great splendor along with the women's quarters. She was entrusted to <s>Mahānāma</s>'s chief queen. She said: 'Your Majesty, a name should be established for her.' <s>Mahānāma</s> said: 'This girl was obtained from the mango grove. He told them: 'Go to <s>Saralaka</s> mountain and bring back something that is not medicine.' They went, and whatever was not medicine to them, they took. <s>Jīvaka</s> reflected: 'There is nothing that is not medicine.' He took a reed-root and a stone roller. Meanwhile, on the way back, <s>Jīvaka</s> saw a cowherd woman who had taken a curd-pot and a lump of alkali and was heading toward <s>Ātreya</s>, suffering severely from eye disease. He asked her: 'Where are you going?' She told him. He prescribed medicine for her right there on the spot from the remedies at hand. She used it and immediately recovered. Delighted, she said: 'Here is your curd-pot and lump of alkali.' He took the alkali lump, but the curd-pot was given to her [back]. He (

children.text: ) kiṭālapiṇḍam ādāya saṃprasthitaḥ / yāvat tair māṇavakair antarmārge hastipadaṃ dṛṣṭam* / te taṃ nirīkṣitum ārabdhāḥ / jīvakaś cāgataḥ kathayati / kim etat* / hastipadam* / naitad dhastipadam* / hastinyā etat padam* / sā ca dakṣiṇakāṇādyaiva kalabhakaṃ janayiṣyati / tatra strī abhirūḍhā / sāpi dakṣiṇakāṇā / gurviṇī / adyaiva putraṃ janayiṣyati / yāvad ātreyasakāśaṃ gataḥ / yena yadānītaṃ tat tenopadarśitam* / ātreyaḥ kathayati / māṇavakāḥ sarvam etad bhaiṣajyam etan tāvad udakenaivaṃ vidhināmukasya rogasya / evam anyāny apīti / jīvakaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ / tvayā kim ānītam* / sa kathayaty upādhyāya sarvam eva bhaiṣajyaṃ nāsti kiñcid abhaiṣajyam* / api tu mayā śaramūlam ānītaṃ pāṣāṇavartikā kiṭālapiṇḍaś ceti / kim ebhiḥ prayojanam* / śaramūlair vṛścikaviddhasya dhūpo dīyate / kiṭālapiṇḍenopanāho dīyate / pāṣāṇaśarkarayā kāle dadhighaṭakā bhidyante / ātreyeṇa vipuṣpitam* / māṇavakāḥ saṃlakṣayanty upādhyāyo 'sya ruṣita iti / te kathayanty upādhyāya kim etad eva / asmābhir āgacchadbhir antarmārge hastipadaṃ dṛṣṭam* / eṣa kathayati / hastinyā etat padam* / sā ca dakṣiṇakāṇā / gurviṇī / adyaiva prasaviṣyati / kalabhakaṃ janayiṣyati / strī tatrābhirūḍhā / sāpi dakṣiṇakāṇā / gurviṇī / adyaiva prasaviṣyati / putraṃ janayiṣyatīti / (
children.translated_text: ) set off with the alkali lump. Meanwhile, on the road, the students saw an elephant's footprint. They began to examine it. <s>Jīvaka</s> arrived and asked: 'What is this?' 'An elephant's footprint.' 'This is not an elephant's footprint. It is a she-elephant's print. She is blind in the right eye. She will give birth to a calf this very day. A woman is riding upon her. She too is blind in the right eye. She is pregnant. She too will give birth to a son this very day.' Then they went to <s>Ātreya</s>. Each showed what he had brought. <s>Ātreya</s> said: 'Students, all this is medicine—this much by this method [cures] such-and-such a disease, and so on for the others.' <s>Jīvaka</s> was asked: 'What did you bring?' He said: 'Teacher, everything is medicine; there is nothing that is not medicine. But I brought a reed-root, a stone roller, and an alkali lump.' 'What use are these?' 'Reed-roots are used for fumigation of scorpion stings. An alkali lump is used for poultices. A stone pebble is used to break curd-pots when the time comes.' <s>Ātreya</s> blossomed [with delight]. The students thought the teacher was angry with him. They said: 'Teacher, is this all? As we were coming back, we saw an elephant's footprint on the road. He says: "This is the print of a she-elephant. She is blind in the right eye. She is pregnant. She will give birth today. She will produce a calf. A woman is riding on her. She too is blind in the right eye. She is pregnant. She too will give birth today. She will produce a son."' (

children.text: ) kathaṃ na jānīmaḥ / hastipadaṃ parimaṇḍalaṃ hastinyās tu dīrgham* / kathaṃ jñāyate dakṣiṇakāṇeti / vāmena pārśvena carantī gatā / kathaṃ jñāyate gurviṇīti / paścimau pādau nipīḍayanti gatā / kathaṃ jñāyate 'dyaiva prasaviṣyatīti / saśukraprasrāvaḥ kṛtaḥ / kathaṃ jñāyate kalabhakaṃ prasaviṣyatīti / bhūyasā dakṣiṇaṃ pādam abhipīḍayantī gatā / kathaṃ jñāyate tatra strī abhirūḍheti / avatīrya pādayor madhye prasrāvaḥ kṛtaḥ / kathaṃ jñāyate sāpi dakṣiṇakāṇeti / vāmena pārśvena puṣpāṇy ucinvantī gacchati / kathaṃ jñāyate sāpi gurviṇīti / bhūyasā pārṣṇiṃ nipīḍayantī gatā / kathaṃ jñāyate 'dyaiva prasaviṣyatīti / saśukraprasrāvaḥ kṛtaḥ / api tu yady upādhyāyasya vimarṣaḥ sa sārtho 'muṣmin pradeśe tatra kañcin māṇavaṃ preṣaya / tena māṇavaḥ preṣitaḥ / sarvaṃ tathaiva yathā jīvakena samākhyātam* / ātreyo māṇavakān āmantrayate / māṇavakāḥ śrutaṃ vaḥ / upādhyāya śrutam* / idṛśo jīvakaḥ prājñaḥ /
children.translated_text: ) How would we not know? An elephant's footprint is round, but a she-elephant's is elongated.' 'How is it known she is blind in the right eye?' 'She walked grazing on the left side.' 'How is it known she is pregnant?' 'She walked pressing down her hind feet.' 'How is it known she will give birth today?' 'She has discharged fluid mixed with semen.' 'How is it known she will produce a calf?' 'She walked pressing down the right foot more heavily.' 'How is it known a woman is riding on her?' 'Having dismounted, she urinated between her feet.' 'How is it known she too is blind in the right eye?' 'She walked picking flowers on the left side.' 'How is it known she too is pregnant?' 'She walked pressing down her heel more heavily.' 'How is it known she too will give birth today?' 'She has discharged fluid mixed with semen.' 'Moreover, if the Teacher has doubts, that caravan is at such-and-such a place—send a student there.' He sent a student. Everything was exactly as <s>Jīvaka</s> had reported. <s>Ātreya</s> addressed the students: 'Students, did you hear?' 'Teacher, we heard.' 'Such is <s>Jīvaka</s>'s intelligence.'

body.translated_text: King <s>Bimbisāra</s> was exceedingly fond of other men's wives. Mounted on the back of an elephant, he would roam through the streets of the city, gazing about with wandering eyes. At that time, in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, there was a certain guild-master — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions. He had brought a wife from a family equal to his own. He enjoyed her company as before. On another occasion, he addressed his wife: 'Dear one, I am going to another country with merchandise.' She said: 'Noble husband, do so.' He went to another country with his merchandise. She, with loosened garments, began to be troubled by desires. King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, mounted on the back of an elephant, was passing near her house. She, standing at the window, threw a garland toward the king. Then the king saw her and said: 'Come.' She said: 'Your Majesty, I am embarrassed. You yourself come in.' Then the king entered. He enjoyed her company. At that time, the fortunate woman, being in her fertile period, became pregnant. She informed the king: 'Your Majesty, I have become pregnant.' Then the king gave her too a signet ring and a distinctive cloth, and said: 'If a boy is born, wrap him in this cloth, tie the signet ring around his neck, and send him to me. But if a girl, she is yours.' The king departed. After some time, that caravan-leader returned with his business completed to the vicinity of <s>Rājagṛha</s>. He sent word to his wife: 'Dear one, rejoice! I have returned safely with my business completed. In how many days (

body.text: jīvakena sarvaṃ śikṣitaṃ sthāpayitvā kapālamocanīṃ vidyām* / yāvad anyatamaḥ puruṣaḥ kapālavyādhinā spṛṣṭa ātreyasakāśaṃ gataḥ kathayaty ātreya mama cikitsāṃ kuru / sa kathayati / bhoḥ puruṣa adya tāvad gartāṃ khānaya gomayaṃ ca samupānaya / śvo 'haṃ tava cikitsāṃ karomīti / jīvakena śrutam* / sa tasya pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhaḥ / bhoḥ (

children.text: ) puruṣa yat kiṃcid ahaṃ śikṣe sarvaṃ tat satvahitahetoḥ / mayā kapālamocanī na śikṣitā / sa tvaṃ samprati gupte sthāpaya yathā tava karma kriyamāṇaṃ paśyāmīti / sa kathayati / tathā bhavatv iti / sa tena pratigupte pradeśe sthāpitaḥ / tata ātreyeṇāgatya sa puruṣo gartāyāṃ nikhātaḥ / kapālamocanyā vidyayā kapālaṃ mocitam* / sa taṃ prāṇakaṃ saṃdaṃśena grahītum ārabdhaḥ / jīvakaḥ kathayaty upādhyāya mā sāhasaṃ kariṣyasi / adyaivāyaṃ kulaputraḥ kālaṃ kariṣyatīti / sa kathayati / jīvaka āgato 'si / sa kathayati / upādhyāyāgato 'ham* / tat katham ayaṃ prāṇakair grahītavyaḥ / upādhyāya saṃdaṃśaṃ tāpayitvā pṛṣṭhe spṛśa / pādau saṃkocayiṣyati / tato 'panayiṣyasīti / tena tathā kṛtam* / svasthībhūtaḥ / ātreyaḥ kathayati / jīvaka parituṣṭo 'haṃ snātvāgaccha kapālamocanīṃ vidyāṃ dāsyāmīti / sa snātvāgataḥ / tena tasya kapālamocanī vidyā dattā / uktañ ca / jīvakāsmākaṃ jīvikaiṣā na tvayeha viṣaye prayoktavyā / upādhyāya tathā bhavatu / jīvaka ātreyam upāmaṃtrya puṣkarasāriṇo rājñaḥ sakāśaṃ gatvopāmaṃtrayati / mayā vaidyakaṃ śikṣitam* / gacchāmīti / tena khalu samayena puṣkarasāriṇo rājñaḥ pāṇḍavā nāma khaṣā viruddhāḥ / (
children.translated_text: ) man, whatever I learn is all for the benefit of living beings. I have not learned the skull-opening technique. You now place me in a hidden spot so that I may observe your procedure.' He said: 'So be it.' He was placed in a concealed spot. Then <s>Ātreya</s> came and buried that man in the pit. With the skull-opening technique, he opened the skull. He began to grasp the creature with forceps. <s>Jīvaka</s> said: 'Teacher, do not act rashly! This young man will die this very day.' He said: '<s>Jīvaka</s>, you have come!' He replied: 'Teacher, I have come. But how should this creature be grasped? Teacher, heat the forceps and touch his back; he will contract his legs, and then you can remove him.' He did so. The patient recovered. <s>Ātreya</s> said: '<s>Jīvaka</s>, I am pleased. Bathe and come; I shall give you the skull-opening technique.' He bathed and came. He gave him the skull-opening technique. And he said: '<s>Jīvaka</s>, this is our livelihood; you must not use it in this region.' 'Teacher, so be it.' <s>Jīvaka</s>, having taken leave of <s>Ātreya</s>, went to King <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> and took his leave: 'I have learned the medical art; I am departing.' Now at that time, the <s>Pāṇḍava Khaṣas</s> were in revolt against King <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>. (

children.text: ) sa kathayati / jīvaka mama pāṇḍavā nāma khaṣā viruddhāṃs tāvat saṃnāmaya paścād yāsyasi / evam asmākaṃ lokayātrā kṛtā bhavati / yasmāt tvaṃ prājñaḥ śaktaś ceti / tena tasya pratijñātam* / tatas tena caturaṃgaṃ balakāyaṃ datvā preṣitaḥ / tena te pāṇḍavāḥ khaṣāḥ sannāmitāḥ / vandigograhakarapratyāyāṃś ca gṛhītvā svastitaḥ pratyāgataḥ / yathānītaṃ ca rājñe upanāmitam* / tena parituṣṭena tasyaivānumoditam* tenāpi ātreyāya dattam* /
children.translated_text: ) He said: '<s>Jīvaka</s>, first subdue my rebellious <s>Pāṇḍava Khaṣas</s>; after that you may go. In this way our worldly obligation will be fulfilled, since you are intelligent and capable.' <s>Jīvaka</s> agreed. Then, having given him a four-division army, he sent him. He subdued those <s>Pāṇḍava Khaṣas</s>. Having collected tributes, tribute-cattle, and revenues, he returned safely. He presented everything as brought to the king. The pleased king gave it all back to him, and he in turn gave it to <s>Ātreya</s>.

body.translated_text: <s>Jīvaka</s> had learned everything except the skull-opening technique. Now, a certain man, afflicted with a skull disease, went to <s>Ātreya</s> and said: '<s>Ātreya</s>, treat me.' He replied: 'Good man, today first dig a pit and bring cow dung. Tomorrow I shall treat you.' <s>Jīvaka</s> heard this. He followed behind him: 'Good (

body.text: tato jīvako 'nupūrveṇa bhadraṃkaraṃ nagaram anuprāptaḥ / tatraiva varṣārātram avasthitam* / tatra tena sarvabhūtarutaṃ nāma śāstraṃ śikṣitam* / sa bhadraṃkarān nagarāt saṃprasthitaḥ / (

children.text: ) anyatamaś ca puruṣaḥ kāṣṭhabhāram ādāya nagaraṃ praviśaty asthicarmāvaśeṣaḥ samantād gātreṇādharataḥ / sa jīvakena dṛṣṭa uktaś ca / bhoḥ puruṣa kena te īdṛśī samavasthā iti / sa kathayaty aham api na jāne / api tu mayā caiṣa cāṣṭhabhārako gṛhīto bhavati / mama cedṛśī samavasthā iti / sa dāruparīkṣāyāṃ kṛtāvī / sa kathayati / bhoḥ puruṣa kim ayaṃ kāṣṭhabhārako vikrīyate / vikrīyate / kiyatā mūlyena / paṃcabhiḥ kārṣāpaṇaśataiḥ / tenāsau krītaḥ / tataḥ pratyavekṣatā sarvabhūtaprasādano nāma maṇir dṛṣṭaḥ / tasyedṛśaḥ prabhāvo yadā vyādhitasya purastāt sthāpyate tadā vyādhir yathābhūtā ca dṛśyate pradīpeṇeva gṛhagataṃ dravyam* /
children.translated_text: ) A certain man, carrying a load of firewood, was entering the city—reduced to nothing but bones and skin, his limbs wasted all around. <s>Jīvaka</s> saw him and asked: 'Good man, how have you come to this condition?' He replied: 'I do not know myself. But ever since I took up this load of firewood, this has been my condition.' <s>Jīvaka</s> was skilled in the examination of wood. He said: 'Good man, is this load of firewood for sale?' 'It is for sale.' 'At what price?' 'Five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>.' He bought it. Then, examining it, he found a jewel called <s>Sarvabhūtaprasādana</s> (the Pacifier of All Beings). Its power was such that when placed before a sick person, the disease was seen as it truly was, like objects in a house seen by lamplight.

body.translated_text: Then <s>Jīvaka</s>, proceeding by stages, reached the city of <s>Bhadraṅkara</s>. He stayed there for the rain-season. There he learned the treatise called 'The Cries of All Beings.' He departed from the city of <s>Bhadraṅkara</s>. (

body.text: so 'nupūrveṇa udumbarikām anuprāptaḥ / tatrānyatama āḍhakamāpakaḥ puruṣaḥ / sa droṇaṃ māpayitvāḍhakena śirasi prahāraṃ dadāti / jīvakena dṛṣṭaḥ uktaś ca bhoḥ puruṣa kimartham eva karoṣi / śiro me atīva kaṇḍūyate / āgaccha paśyāmaḥ / tena tasya niṣadya śiro darśitam* / tato jīvakena sarvabhūtaprasādako maṇis tasya śirasi sthāpito yāvat paśyati śatapadīm* / tataḥ kathayati / bhoḥ puruṣa tava śirasi śatapadī tiṣṭhatīti / sa pādayor nipatya kathayati cikitsāṃ me kuruṣveti / tena pratijñātam* / jīvakaḥ saṃlakṣayati / upādhyāyasyaivopadeśena cikitsām asya karomīti / sa tenoktaḥ / bhoḥ puruṣādya gartaṃ khānaya pāṣiṃ ca samupānaya cikitsāṃ kariṣyāmīti / sa padayor nipatya prakrāntaḥ / jīvakenāpy aparasmin divase sa puruṣo garte nikhāte nikhātya kapālamocanyā vidyayā kapālaṃ mocayitvā saptena saṃdaṃśena śatapadī spṛṣṭā / tayā pādāḥ saṃkocitāḥ / tatas tena saṃdaṃśena gṛhītvā kṣiptā / svasthībhūtaḥ / tena tasya paṃca kārṣāpaṇaśatāni dattāni / tenātreyāya preṣitāni /
body.translated_text: He proceeded by stages to <s>Udumbarikā</s>. There, a certain grain-measurer—when he measured a <s>droṇa</s> (a measure), he would strike himself on the head with the <s>āḍhaka</s> measure. <s>Jīvaka</s> saw this and said: 'Good man, why do you do that?' 'My head itches terribly.' 'Come, let me see.' He sat down and showed his head. Then <s>Jīvaka</s> placed the <s>Sarvabhūtaprasādaka</s> jewel on his head, and looking, he saw a centipede. He said: 'Good man, there is a centipede lodged in your head.' The man fell at his feet and said: 'Treat me!' He agreed. <s>Jīvaka</s> considered: 'I shall treat him following my teacher's instructions.' He told him: 'Good man, today dig a pit and bring a shovel; I shall perform the treatment.' The man fell at his feet and departed. The next day, <s>Jīvaka</s> buried that man in the pit, and with the skull-opening technique opened the skull. With a heated forceps he touched the centipede. It contracted its legs. Then, grasping it with the forceps, he removed it. The patient recovered. He gave <s>Jīvaka</s> five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>, which <s>Jīvaka</s> sent to <s>Ātreya</s>.

body.text: tato jīvako rohītakam anuprāptaḥ / rohītake 'nyatamasya gṛhapater udyānaṃ puṣpaphalasalilasaṃpannam* / sa tatrātivādhyavasitaḥ kālaṃ kṛtvā tasminn evāmanuṣyakeṣūpapannaḥ / tasya putro gṛhasvāmī saṃvṛttaḥ / tena tasminn udyāne ārakṣakaḥ puruṣaḥ sthāpitaḥ / sa tenāmanuṣyakeṇa praghātitaḥ / dvitīyaḥ sthāpitaḥ / so 'pi praghātitaḥ / tena gṛhapatiputreṇa (

children.text: ) tad udyānam utsṛṣṭam* / yāvad anyatara udarī manuṣyaḥ sarvavaidyapratyākhyātas tad udyānaṃ gatvā rātriṃ vāsam upagataḥ / aho bata māmanuṣyakaḥ praghātayed iti / tasminn eva ca jīvako rātriṃ vāsam upagataḥ / yāvad asāv amanuṣyakas tam udariṇam abhidravitum ārabdhaḥ / sa jalodaro rogo niṣkramya kathayati / mayāyaṃ pūrvaṃ gṛhītaḥ / kimartham enam abhidravasi / nāsti te kaścit* chāgasaṭāyā dhūpaṃ dātā yena tvaṃ dvādaśa yojanāni niṣpalāyer iti / so 'pi kathayati / tavāpi nāsti kaścin mūlakabījam udaśvinā piṣṭā dātā yena tvaṃ khaṇḍaṃ khaṇḍaṃ viśīryethā iti / jīvakena sarvaṃ śrutam* / sa kalyam evotthāya tasya gṛhapateḥ sakāśaṃ gataḥ / kathayati gṛhapate udyānaṃ puṣpaphalasalilasaṃpannaṃ kimartham utsṛṣṭam iti / gṛhapatināsya yathāvṛttam ārocitam* / sa kathayati / gṛhapate chāgalasaṭāyā dhūpaṃ dehi / (
children.translated_text: ) abandoned that park. Now, a certain man with dropsy, rejected by all physicians, went to that park and spent the night, thinking: 'Oh, if only the non-human being would kill me!' <s>Jīvaka</s> too spent the night in that same place. The non-human being began to attack the man with dropsy. But the disease of dropsy came out and said: 'I seized this one first. Why do you attack him? Is there no one to fumigate you with goat hair, so that you would flee twelve leagues?' And the non-human being replied: 'And is there no one to give you radish seeds ground with water, so that you would disintegrate piece by piece?' <s>Jīvaka</s> heard all this. Rising at dawn, he went to that householder and said: 'Householder, why have you abandoned a park abounding in flowers, fruits, and water?' The householder told him the full account. He said: 'Householder, fumigate with goat hair. (

children.text: ) dvādaśayojanāny amanuṣyako niṣpalāyati / gṛhapatinā chāgalasaṭāyā dhūpo dattaḥ / amanuṣyako dvādaśa yojanāni niṣpalāyitaḥ / tenāpi gṛhapatinā paṃca kārṣāpaṇaśatāni jīvakāya dattāni / tāny api tenātreyāya preṣitāni /
children.translated_text: ) The non-human being will flee twelve leagues.' The householder fumigated with goat hair. The non-human being fled twelve leagues. That householder too gave <s>Jīvaka</s> five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>, which he sent to <s>Ātreya</s>.

body.translated_text: Then <s>Jīvaka</s> reached <s>Rohītaka</s>. At <s>Rohītaka</s>, a certain householder had a park abounding in flowers, fruits, and water. He, being excessively attached to it, died and was reborn as a non-human being in that very place. His son became the owner of the house. He appointed a guard in that park. The guard was killed by that non-human being. A second was appointed; he too was killed. The householder's son (

body.text: tato jīvako 'nupūrveṇa mathurām anuprāptaḥ / bahir mathurāyā vṛkṣamūle viśrāntaḥ / yāvan mallena mallo nihataḥ / tasyāntrāṇi parāvṛttāni / sa mṛta iti bahir niṣkāsyate / tasmiṃś ca vṛkṣe vṛdhriṇī sapotakā tiṣṭhati / sā taiḥ potakair ucyate / amba māṃsam anuprayaccheti / sā kathayati / putra kuto māṃsam* / te kathayanti / amba eṣa mallo mallena nihataḥ kālagato nīyate / putra jīvako 'tra vaidyarāja āgataḥ / sthānam etad vidyate yad enaṃ svasthīkariṣyati / amba kenaiṣa svastho bhavati / yady asya cūrṇair antrāṇi spṛśyante / jīvakena tat sarvaṃ śrutam* / tato 'sāv utthāya mṛtasakāśaṃ gatvā pṛcchati bhavantaḥ kim etad iti / te kathayanti / mallena mallo nihataḥ / kālagataḥ / jīvakaḥ kathayati / sthāpayata / paśyāmi / taiḥ sthāpitam* / tato jīvakena ca sarvabhūtaprasādakamaṇiḥ śirasi sthāpayitvā pratyavekṣitaḥ / yāvat paśyaty antrāṇi vyākulīkṛtāni / tena nāḍikāyāṃ cūrṇaṃ prakṣipya mukhe vāyunā preritam* / cūrṇenāntrāṇi spṛṣṭāni / svasthībhūtaḥ / tenāpi jīvakasya paṃca kārṣāpaṇaśatāni dattāni / tenāpy ātreyāya preṣitāni /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Jīvaka</s>, proceeding by stages, reached <s>Mathurā</s>. He rested at the foot of a tree outside <s>Mathurā</s>. A wrestler was killed by another wrestler. His intestines were displaced. He was being carried out as dead. In that tree lived a female vulture with her chicks. They said to her: 'Mother, give us meat.' She said: 'Children, where is there meat?' They said: 'Mother, this wrestler was killed by a wrestler and has died; he is being carried away.' 'Children, <s>Jīvaka</s>, the king of physicians, has come here. It is possible that he will cure him.' 'Mother, how can he be cured?' 'If his intestines are touched with powders.' <s>Jīvaka</s> heard all this. Then he rose and went to the dead man and asked: 'Gentlemen, what is this?' They said: 'A wrestler was killed by a wrestler; he has died.' <s>Jīvaka</s> said: 'Set him down; let me look.' They set him down. Then <s>Jīvaka</s>, placing the <s>Sarvabhūtaprasādaka</s> jewel on his head, examined him. He saw that the intestines were disarranged. He put powder into a tube and blew it into the mouth with air. The powder touched the intestines. The man recovered. He too gave <s>Jīvaka</s> five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>, which he sent to <s>Ātreya</s>.

body.text: mathurāyām anyatamo gṛhapatiḥ / tasya patnī rūpayauvanasaṃpannā / sa tasyām atyartham adhyavasitaḥ kālagataḥ / tasyām eva yonau kṛmiḥ prādurbhūtaḥ / sā yena sārdhaṃ paricārayati sa kālaṃ karoti / tatas tayā sārdhaṃ na kaścit paricārayati / tayā śrutaṃ jīvako vaidya ihāgataḥ iti / sā tasya sakāśaṃ gatvā kathayati / jīvaka mama vyādhir asti / cikitsāṃ kuru / jīvakas tāṃ dṛṣṭvā kathālāpaṃ ca śrutvā saṃraktaḥ kathayati / samayataḥ cikitsāṃ karomi yadi ca mayā sārdhaṃ paricārayasīti / sā kathayati / jihremi / sa kathayati / nāsti te 'nyathā cikitsā / nāsty ātmasamaṃ prema / tayā pratijñātam* / tatas tayātmanā nagnībhūtā / yonidvāre māṃsapeśī dattā / tato 'sau kṛmis tasyāṃ lagnaḥ / sa tena gṛhītvā kṣiptaḥ / svasthībhūtā / sā kāmarāgādhyavasitā nimittam upadarśayati / sa karṇau pidhāya kathayati bhaginī tvaṃ mama / tavaiṣā cikitseti mayaivaṃ kṛtam iti / tayā tasmai paṃca kārṣāpaṇaśatāni dattāni / tāny apy tenātreyāya preṣitāni /
body.translated_text: In <s>Mathurā</s> there was a certain householder. His wife was endowed with beauty and youth. He, being excessively attached to her, died. A worm was born in that very womb. Whoever consorted with her died. Therefore no one would consort with her. She heard that <s>Jīvaka</s> the physician had come there. She went to him and said: '<s>Jīvaka</s>, I have an illness; treat me.' <s>Jīvaka</s>, seeing her and hearing her conversation, became enamored and said: 'I shall treat you on one condition—that you consort with me.' She said: 'I am ashamed.' He said: 'There is no other treatment for you; there is no love equal to self-love.' She agreed. Then, having herself become naked, she placed a piece of meat at the opening of the womb. The worm attached itself to it. He seized it and removed it. She recovered. She, overcome with desire, made signs of invitation. He, covering his ears, said: 'Sister, you are my sister. This was your treatment—that is why I did this.' She gave him five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>, which he sent to <s>Ātreya</s>.

It was opening and closing its eyes. <s>Jīvaka</s> observed everything—how the sinews, joints, and ankle-structures of the body (

body.text: so 'nupūrveṇa vaiśālīṃ gataḥ / yāvan mallena mallasya talaprahāreṇākṣipelāṃkolaṃbhitaḥ / sa jīvakasya sakāśaṃ gataḥ / tena tasyāṃ pārṣṇyāṃ snāyujālam ākṛṣya praveśitam* / tena tasya paṃca kārṣāpaṇaśatāni dattāni / tenābhayasya mātur dattāni /
body.translated_text: He proceeded by stages to <s>Vaiśālī</s>. A wrestler, struck by another wrestler's palm-blow, had his ankle dislocated. He went to <s>Jīvaka</s>. <s>Jīvaka</s> pulled the sinew-network in that heel and reinserted it. He gave <s>Jīvaka</s> five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>, which <s>Jīvaka</s> gave to <s>Abhaya</s>'s mother.

body.text: vaiśālyām anyatamaḥ puruṣaḥ / tasya śatapadī karṇaṃ praviṣṭā / sā tatra prasutā / saptaśatāny apatyānāṃ jātāni / sa karṇaśūlābhyāhato jīvakasya sakāśaṃ gataḥ / cikitsāṃ kuruṣveti / jīvakaḥ saṃlakṣayati / pūrvaṃ mayā upādhyāyopadeśena karma kṛtam idānīṃ svamatena karma kariṣyāmīti / tenāsau puruṣo 'bhihitaḥ / gaccha bhoḥ puruṣa patramaṇḍapaṃ kārayata / nīlair vastrair veṣṭayitvāsyādhastād bherīṃ sthāpaya / bhṛmiṃ ca tāpaya iti / tena yathāsaṃdiṣṭaṃ sarvam anuṣṭhitam* / tato jīvakena taṃ puruṣaṃ bhūmau nipātayitvā sā bhūmir udakena siktā / tato bherī parāhatā / śatapadī prāvṛṭkāla iti kṛtvā niṣkrāntā / tato jīvakena karṇamūle māṃsapeśī sthāpitā / sā punaḥ praviṣyāpatyāni gṛhītvā nirgatā / sahāpatyair māṃsapeśyāṃ siktā / tato jīvakena sā māṃsapeśīcchoritā / sa puruṣa svasthībhūtaḥ / tena paṃca kārṣāpaṇaśatāni dattāni / tāny api tenābhayasya mātur dattāni /
body.translated_text: In <s>Vaiśālī</s> there was a certain man. A centipede had entered his ear. It bred there; seven hundred offspring were born. Afflicted by earache, he went to <s>Jīvaka</s>: 'Treat me.' <s>Jīvaka</s> considered: 'Previously I performed procedures following my teacher's instructions; now I shall perform a procedure according to my own judgment.' He told the man: 'Go, good man, have a pavilion of leaves made. Cover it with blue cloths and place a drum underneath. And heat an iron rod.' Everything was arranged as instructed. Then <s>Jīvaka</s> laid the man on the ground and sprinkled that ground with water. Then the drum was struck. The centipede, thinking it was the rainy season, came out. Then <s>Jīvaka</s> placed a piece of meat at the ear opening. The centipede re-entered, gathered its offspring, and came out. Together with its offspring, it was dropped onto the piece of meat. Then <s>Jīvaka</s> flicked away the piece of meat. The man recovered. He gave five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>, which <s>Jīvaka</s> gave to <s>Abhaya</s>'s mother.

body.text: so 'nupūrveṇa rājagṛhaṃ gataḥ / rājñā bimbisāreṇa śrutaṃ yathā jīvaka āgata iti / tenājātaśatroḥ kumārasyājñā dattā putra bhrātā te āgacchati pratyudgamako gaccheti / sa pratyudgataḥ / jīvakena śrutaṃ yathā ajātaśatruḥ kumāraḥ pratyudgacchatīti / sa saṃlakṣayati / yady aham asya pratyudgamanaṃ svīkariṣyāmīti yadā rājā bhaviṣyati tadānarthaṃ me kariṣyatīti / sa parāvṛtyānyena dvāreṇa praviṣṭaḥ / apareṇa samayena jīvako mahājanakāyaparivṛto vyākṣiptacitto gacchati / tāvad anyataro brāhmaṇo 'kṣirogārto jīvakasya sakāśaṃ gataḥ / bhaiṣajyaṃ me vyapadiśeti / tena saṃjātāmarṣeṇoktaḥ / bhasmanā pūraya iti / tena ṛjukena bhasmanā pūritam* / svasthībhūtaḥ /
body.translated_text: He went by stages to <s>Rājagṛha</s>. King <s>Bimbisāra</s> heard that <s>Jīvaka</s> had arrived. He gave an order to Prince <s>Ajātaśatru</s>: 'Son, your brother is coming—go out to welcome him.' He went out to meet him. <s>Jīvaka</s> heard that Prince <s>Ajātaśatru</s> was coming to meet him. He reflected: 'If I accept his welcome, then when he becomes king, he will cause me harm.' He turned back and entered through another gate. On another occasion, <s>Jīvaka</s>, surrounded by a great multitude of people, was going about with a distracted mind. Just then, a certain Brahmin afflicted with an eye disease went to <s>Jīvaka</s> and said: 'Prescribe medicine for me.' <s>Jīvaka</s>, having become irritated, said: 'Fill it with ashes.' He, taking it literally, filled [his eyes] with ashes. He was cured.

body.text: aparasyāpy akṣirogaḥ / sa jīvakasakāśaṃ saṃprasthitaḥ / tena brāhmaṇena dṛṣṭaḥ pṛṣṭaś ca / bhoḥ puruṣa kva gacchasīti / tena yathābhūtam ākhyātam* / sa kathayati / kiṃ te jīvakena / yat tena mamopadiṣṭaṃ tat kuruṣveti / śraddadhāno 'sau / tena bhasmanā pūrite andhībhūtaḥ /
body.translated_text: Another person also had an eye disease. He set out toward <s>Jīvaka</s>. That Brahmin saw him and asked: 'Good sir, where are you going?' He told him the truth. The Brahmin said: 'What do you need <s>Jīvaka</s> for? Do what he prescribed for me.' Trusting him, when he filled [his eyes] with ashes, he became blind.

children.text: ) tāvad rājñā bhuktam* / jīvaka cikitsāṃ kuru / deva kṛtā / sa tadante pāṇinā parāmārṣṭi / na saṃjānīte katarasmin pradeśe vraṇam iti / ādarśaṃ gṛhītvā vyavalokayati tathāpi na paśyati / devīṃ pṛcchati / sāpi na saṃjānīte katarasmin pradeśe vraṇam āsīd iti / rājā paraṃ vismayam āpanna amātyānāṃ kathayati / bhavato jīvakasya vaidyarājābhiṣekaṃ kuruteti / so 'ndhaḥ puruṣaḥ kathayati / deva kiṃ putrasnehād asyābhiṣekaḥ kriyate / āhosvid vaidyavaicakṣaṇyād iti / sa kathayati / vaidyacaikṣaṇyāt* / yady evam aham evānenāndhīkṛtaḥ / jīvakaḥ kathayati / bhoḥ puruṣa tavāhaṃ darśanam api na samanupaśyāmi kutaḥ svasthīkariṣyāmi / sa kathayati / satyam etad api tu yasya tvayopadeśaḥ kṛtas tena mamopadiṣṭam* / kim upadiṣṭam* / amukam* / jīvakaḥ kathayati / tasyānyo dhātuḥ / tavāpy anyaḥ / idānīm idaṃ cedaṃ ca kuru / svasthībhaviṣyasīti / tena kṛtam* / (
children.translated_text: ) The king ate. '<s>Jīvaka</s>, perform the treatment.' 'Your Majesty, it has been done.' At the end of the meal, the king felt with his hand but could not tell in which spot the wound had been. Taking a mirror, he looked—even so, he could not see it. He asked the queen. She too could not tell in which spot the wound had been. The king was filled with the utmost astonishment and said to the ministers: 'Sirs, perform the consecration of <s>Jīvaka</s> as chief physician.' That blind man said: 'Your Majesty, is the consecration being performed out of fatherly affection for him, or out of [recognition of his] medical expertise?' He said: 'Out of medical expertise.' 'If so, it is I who was made blind by him!' <s>Jīvaka</s> said: 'Good sir, I do not even recall having seen you—how could I have cured you?' He said: 'That is true, but the one whose prescription you gave—he advised me.' 'What did he advise?' 'Such-and-such.' <s>Jīvaka</s> said: 'His constitution is different from yours. Yours is also different. Now do this and this, and you will be cured.' He did so. (

body.text: rājagṛhe 'nyatamo gṛhapatir gulmavyādhinā spṛṣṭaḥ / sarvavaidyapratyākhyātaḥ / sa saṃlakṣayati / jīvakasya sakāśaṃ gacchāmīti / yadi cikitsāṃ kariṣyaty atīva kuśalaṃ no ced ātmānaṃ ghātayiṣyāmīti / sa jīvakasakāśaṃ gataḥ / jīvaka cikitsāṃ me kuru / sa kathayati / bhoḥ puruṣa durlabhāni tava bhaiṣajyānīti / sa saṃlakṣayati / jīvakenāpy ahaṃ pratyākhyātaḥ / kim atra prāptakāla ātmānaṃ ghātayiṣyāmīti / śmaśānaṃ gataḥ / tatra citāyāṃ jvalantyāṃ babhrunakulaś candanagodhā ca yudhyamānau patitau / tena kṣudhārtena tāv ubhāv api bhakṣitau / devaś ca vṛṣṭaḥ / śmaśānāt pragharat tac citodakaṃ pītam* / śmaśānasya nātidūre gokulam* / tatra gatvā kodravodanaṃ mathitaṃ ca pītam* / gulmaḥ sphuṭitaḥ / ūrdhvam adhaś ca virikto yathā paurāṇaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ /
body.translated_text: In <s>Rājagṛha</s>, a certain householder was afflicted with a <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumor) disease. He had been given up by all physicians. He reflected: 'I shall go to <s>Jīvaka</s>. If he treats me, that will be very good; if not, I shall kill myself.' He went to <s>Jīvaka</s> and said: '<s>Jīvaka</s>, treat me.' He said: 'Good sir, your medicines are difficult to obtain.' He reflected: 'I have been given up even by <s>Jīvaka</s>. What is left to do? I shall kill myself.' He went to the cremation ground. There, on a burning pyre, a brown mongoose and a sandalwood lizard, fighting each other, had fallen in. He, being hungry, ate them both. And the rain-god rained. The cremation-ground water flowed out, and he drank it. Not far from the cremation ground was a cattle station. Going there, he ate boiled <s>kodrava</s> (millet) rice and drank buttermilk. His tumor burst. He was purged upward and downward and was restored to his former health.

He said: 'What kind of medicines are mine?' <s>Jīvaka</s> said: 'If on the dark fourteenth night, a man who has eaten only one lump of food dies, and at the cremation ground where he is being cremated, a brown mongoose and a sandalwood lizard fall into the pyre—you eat those two. The great god <s>Indra</s> rains. You drink the water that flows from the cremation ground. Then you eat boiled <s>kodrava</s> rice and drink buttermilk. Thus you would be cured—knowing this, I said your medicines are difficult to obtain.' He said: 'Excellent! Well understood! That is exactly what I consumed.' Then, filled with admiration, he said: 'Your Majesty, the consecration as chief physician is fitting for him. Let it be done.' He was consecrated as chief physician a second time.

body.translated_text: On another occasion, a boil appeared on the intimate area of Queen <s>Vaidehī</s>. She reported it to the king. The king told <s>Jīvaka</s>: 'Treat the queen mother.' He agreed. Then, forming sweets into a ball, he gave them to the nurse: 'Have her sit near these.' The nurse seated her near them. <s>Jīvaka</s>, having seen the ball of sweets, determined: 'In that spot.' Then he administered ripening drugs. Knowing it was ripe, he inserted a blade inside the ball of sweets and said to the nurse: 'Have the queen sit near these for a moment. She should sit and hold [her body] in the air.' The nurse did so. At the very moment of the blade's contact (

children.translated_text: ) Then, having taken corpse-flesh and prepared it with special seasonings, he presented it to the king at mealtime. Then King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, having taken the bowl of meat and being about to eat it—<s>Jīvaka</s> snatched it away and struck him on the cheek, saying: 'You wretch! You deprived your righteous father, the <s>Dharma</s>-king, of life! And now you eat your own son's flesh too!' Enraged, the king said: 'If so, why was he killed?' And in his outburst of rage, the tumor burst. He was purged upward and downward. Blood came from his mouth. Seeing which, he fainted and fell to the ground. Then, having revived him with a sprinkling of water, he bathed him and gave him restorative food. He was restored to his former health. Then <s>Jīvaka</s>, taking Prince <s>Udāyibhadra</s> adorned with all ornaments, went before the king. He fell at his feet and said: 'Your Majesty, this is Prince <s>Udāyibhadra</s>. I am not able to deprive even an ant or a termite of life, (

children.text: ) prāg eva kumāram* / api tv anenopāyena cikitseti mayopāyasaṃvidhānaṃ kṛtam iti / rājā paraṃ vismayam upagataḥ / tenāmātyānām ājñā dattā / jīvakasya vaidyarājābhiṣekaṃ kuruṣveti / amātyair hastaskandhābhirūḍho mahatā śrīsamudayena trir api vaidyarājābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ /

He gave an order to the ministers: 'Perform the consecration of <s>Jīvaka</s> as chief physician.' The ministers, having him mounted on an elephant, with great pomp and splendor, consecrated him as chief physician for the third time.

body.translated_text: When <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, instigated by <s>Devadatta</s> as his evil friend, deprived his righteous father, the <s>Dharma</s>-king, of life, a <s>gulma</s> (tumor) disease arose in him. He gave an order to the physicians: 'Perform the treatment.' They said: 'Your Majesty, <s>Jīvaka</s> is the supreme chief physician and Your Majesty's brother. While he is present, what ability do we have to treat you?' He gave an order to the ministers: 'Sirs, summon <s>Jīvaka</s>.' They summoned him. '<s>Jīvaka</s>, a tumor disease has arisen in me. Treat it.' 'Your Majesty, I shall.' He reflected: 'A tumor is burst by two causes—either by extreme joy or by extreme rage. This is a sinful being. Whence would he have extreme joy? He must certainly be enraged.' Having determined this, he said: 'Your Majesty, I shall treat you on one condition—if you eat the flesh of Prince <s>Udāyibhadra</s>.' Hearing this, the king was enraged and said: 'Excellent! I have deprived my father of life. You too should deprive <s>Udāyibhadra</s> of life. And I myself shall die of the disease. You too shall become king!' He said: 'Your Majesty, this is the treatment. It is not possible to be cured otherwise.' There is no love equal to self-love. He consented. Then <s>Jīvaka</s> adorned Prince <s>Udāyibhadra</s> with all ornaments and presented him before the king. 'Your Majesty, this is Prince <s>Udāyibhadra</s>. Look at him well—you will not see him again.' Then, having shown him, he took him home and kept him safe. Then <s>Jīvaka</s>, wanting meat, went to the <s>Śītavana</s> cremation ground. And the <s>Śītavana</s> cremation ground was never empty of dead corpses. (

He went, and <s>Jīvaka</s> gathered various kinds of medicinal herbs. The <s>Bhagavān</s> asked: '<s>Jīvaka</s>, what is the name of this herb?' He replied: 'Lord, it is such-and-such. By this method it is a remedy for such-and-such a disease.' 'This one too is such-and-such, a remedy for such-and-such a disease.' But the names of some others he did not know. Those he did not know, the <s>Bhagavān</s> told him: '<s>Jīvaka</s>, this is such-and-such. By such-and-such a method it is a remedy for such-and-such a disease. This one too is for such-and-such.' <s>Jīvaka</s> said: 'Does the <s>Bhagavān</s> also know the science of medicine?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed <s>Jīvaka</s>, the king of physicians: '<s>Jīvaka</s>, a physician-surgeon endowed with four qualities

children.text: ) bhiṣak chalyāhartā rājārhaś ca bhavati rājayogyaś ca rājāṅgatve ca saṃkhyāṃ gacchati / katamaiś caturbhir iha bhiṣak chalyāhartā / ābādhakuśalo bhavati / ābādhasamutthānakuśalaś ca / utpannasyābādhasya prahāṇakuśalaḥ / prahīṇasyāyatyām anutpādakuśalaḥ / katham ābādhakuśalo bhavati / iha bhiṣak chalyāhartābādhaṃ jānāty ayam ābādha evaṃrūpaś caivaṃrūpaś cety evam ābādhakuśalo bhavati / katham ābādhasamutthānakuśalo bhavati / iha bhiṣak chalyāhartābādhaṃ jānāty ayam ābādho vātasamuttho vā vipattisamuttho vā śleṣmasamuttho vātmopakramiko vā paropakramiko vā sāṃnipātiko vā ṛtupariṇāmiko vety evam ābādhasamutthānakuśalo bhavati / katham utpannasyābādhasya prahāṇakuśalo bhavati / iha bhiṣak chalyāhartābādhaṃ jānāty ayam ābādho 'ṃjanena vā pratyaṃjanena vā vāmanena vā virecanena vordhvavirecanena vādhovirecanena vā nastakarmaṇā vā dhūpadānena vā svedaparikarmaṇā vā prahāsyatīty evam utpannasyābādhasya prahāṇakuśalo bhavati / kathaṃ prahīṇasyābādhasyāyatyām anutpādakuśalo bhavati / iha bhiṣak chalyāhartābādhaṃ jānāty ayam ābādha (
children.translated_text: is worthy of a king, fit for a king, and is counted among the king's attendants. Which four? Here, a physician-surgeon is skilled in [diagnosing] illness. He is skilled in [knowing] the origin of illness. He is skilled in curing an arisen illness. He is skilled in preventing the recurrence of a cured illness in the future. How is he skilled in illness? Here, a physician-surgeon knows the illness: "This illness is of such-and-such a form and such-and-such a form"—thus he is skilled in illness. How is he skilled in the origin of illness? Here, a physician-surgeon knows the illness: "This illness arises from wind, or from disorder, or from phlegm, or is self-inflicted, or inflicted by another, or is due to a combination [of humors], or is due to seasonal change"—thus he is skilled in the origin of illness. How is he skilled in curing an arisen illness? Here, a physician-surgeon knows the illness: "This illness will be cured by ointment, or by counter-ointment, or by emetics, or by purgatives, or by upper purgation, or by lower purgation, or by nasal treatment, or by fumigation, or by sweating therapy"—thus he is skilled in curing an arisen illness. children.translated_text: Thus, a physician-surgeon endowed with four qualities is worthy of a king, fit for a king, and is counted among the king's attendants. In just this way, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is called the supreme physician-surgeon, endowed with four qualities. Which four? Here, <s>Jīvaka</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, knows as it truly is: "This is the Noble Truth of suffering." He knows as it truly is: "This is the origin of suffering; this is the cessation of suffering; this is the path leading to the cessation of suffering—the Noble Truth." Indeed, <s>Jīvaka</s>, a physician-surgeon does not know the remedy for the elimination of sufferings rooted in birth. Nor does he know the remedy for the elimination of sufferings rooted in old age, disease, death, grief, lamentation, pain, dejection, and despair. But the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Jīvaka</s>, knows the remedy for the elimination of sufferings rooted in birth. He knows the remedy for the elimination of sufferings rooted in old age, disease, death, grief, lamentation, pain, dejection, and despair. Therefore the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is called the supreme physician-surgeon. When this discourse on the Dharma was being spoken, the dust-free, stainless Dharma-eye arose in <s>Jīvaka Kumārabhṛta</s> regarding phenomena. Then <s>Jīvaka Kumārabhṛta</s>, having seen the Dharma, having attained the Dharma, having understood the Dharma, having penetrated the Dharma, having crossed beyond doubt, having gone beyond uncertainty, having attained confidence in the Teacher's teaching without relying on others, rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, and with joined palms bowed toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> and said: 'I am devoted, Venerable Sir, deeply devoted! I go for refuge to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, to the Dharma, and to the community of monks, and [I declare myself] a lay devotee. May you remember me from this day forward
[MSV II 47]

children.text: ) yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇopetaṃ śaraṇagatam abhiprasannam* / atha jīvako vaidyarājo bhagavata pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ /

body.translated_text: Then pride arose in <s>Jīvaka</s>: 'There is no physician equal to me. I am the foremost among healers of the body. The Blessed One too is the foremost among healers of the mind.' On another occasion, he went before the Blessed One. Due to the veil of pride, he did not see the [Four Noble] Truths. The Blessed One reflected: '<s>Jīvaka</s>, the chief physician, has uprooted roots of merit—why does he not see the Truths? Because of the veil of pride. His pride must be removed.' Then the Blessed One addressed <s>Jīvaka</s> the chief physician: '<s>Jīvaka</s>, have you seen the <s>Himavat</s>, king of mountains?' 'No, venerable sir.' 'Take hold of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s robe-corner.' He took hold. Then the Blessed One, taking <s>Jīvaka</s> the chief physician, went to <s>Himavat</s>, king of mountains. There, various herbs were blazing like lamps. The Blessed One said to <s>Jīvaka</s> the chief physician: '<s>Jīvaka</s>, take whatever herbs you desire.' Venerable sir,

body.text: himavān parvatarājo himasaṃyogān nityaṃ śītalo bhagavataḥ sābhiṣyandaṃ glānam utpannam* / jīvako vaidyarājaḥ saṃlakṣayati / svayam evāhaṃ bhagavata upasthānaṃ karomi tadyathā rājñaś cakravartina iti / tato jīvakena dvātriṃśad utpalāni sraṃsanīyair dravyair bhāvayitvā bhagavate dattāni / jighratu bhagavān etānīti / bhagavatā ghrātāni / dvātriṃśad evotthānāni labdhāni / tato bhagavantaṃ pṛcchati / kaścid bhagavān samyagvirikta iti / bhagavān āha / santi jīvaka te doṣāḥ / ye cyutā na srutāḥ santi / srutā na cyutāḥ santi / srutāś cyutāś ca santi / naiva srutā na cyutā iti / jīvakaḥ kathayati / bhagavan yady evaṃ guḍaharītakīṃ bhakṣaya / maṇḍānupūrvīṃ ca kuruṣveti / bhagavatā tathākṛtam* svastho jātaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Himavān</s>, king of mountains, being always cold due to contact with snow—a phlegmatic illness arose in the <s>Bhagavān</s>. <s>Jīvaka</s>, the king of physicians, reflected: 'I myself shall attend upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>, just as one would attend upon a universal monarch.' Then <s>Jīvaka</s> prepared thirty-two lotuses infused with purgative substances and offered them to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> smell these.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> smelled them, and thirty-two evacuations occurred. Then he asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Has the <s>Bhagavān</s> been properly purged?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'There are, <s>Jīvaka</s>, those humors which have shifted but not discharged; those which have discharged but not shifted; those which have both shifted and discharged; and those which have neither discharged nor shifted.' <s>Jīvaka</s> said: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, if so, please take <s>guḍaharītakī</s> (jaggery and myrobalan), and follow a sequence of gruels.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> did so and was restored to health.

children.translated_text: <s>Jīvaka Kumārabhṛta</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'It is my custom, Venerable Sir, that whenever I treat any king or minister, he gives me a village or a choice village. I treated the king of <s>Videha</s>, and he gave me a large cloak worth a hundred thousand [coins]. I wish to offer it to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept it out of compassion.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> accepted the large cloak worth a hundred thousand from <s>Jīvaka Kumārabhṛta</s>. At that time, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> was standing behind the <s>Bhagavān</s>, holding a fan and fanning the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Take the large cloak worth a hundred thousand, <s>Ānanda</s>, and cut it up for my use.' Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> took it, went to a spacious stretch of ground, and began to measure it. He saw that many robes could be made from it. He made a set of three robes for the <s>Bhagavān</s>, an upper and inner garment for himself, and a <s>kusūlaka</s> (storage bag) for the Venerable <s>Rāhula</s>. During that rainy season, five hundred pieces of cloth came for the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and many for the community of monks. The monks did not know how to deal with them. The monks reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore I permit this: monks should wear householder-cloth robes that are cut with a blade and dyed to a dull color.'

body.translated_text: It was King <s>Bimbisāra</s>'s custom that whenever he saw a monk or a nun, he would dismount from his elephant and perform a salutation at their feet. On a later occasion, having mounted his elephant, he set out to salute the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet. Along the way he saw an <s>Ājīvaka</s> (naked ascetic). Alarmed and confused, he dismounted from the elephant and fell at his feet. Those who lacked faith thought: 'The king is not only devoted to the monks but also to the <s>Ājīvakas</s>.' But those who had faith thought: 'Surely the king, taking him for a monk, dismounted from the elephant in haste and fell at his feet.' They, of uncertain mind, said to the king: 'To whom did Your Majesty make a salutation?' 'To a disciple of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' 'Sire, that is an <s>Ājīvaka</s>, not a disciple of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Then King <s>Bimbisāra</s> reflected: 'This is what I must do.' He approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he saluted the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet with his head and sat to one side. Seated to one side, King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'It is my custom, Venerable Sir, to dismount from my elephant and perform a salutation at the feet of any monk or nun I see. But I, confused and alarmed, dismounted from the elephant and fell at the feet of an <s>Ājīvaka</s>. Would the <s>Bhagavān</s> please institute some distinguishing mark on the robes of the Noble Ones, out of compassion?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> consented to King <s>Bimbisāra</s>'s request by remaining silent. Then King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, understanding the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s consent through his silence, saluted the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet with his head and departed. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'Listen,

body.translated_text: At that time, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> was standing behind the <s>Bhagavān</s>, holding a fan and fanning the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Have you seen the <s>Vaideha</s> mountain, <s>Ānanda</s>?' 'No, Venerable Sir.' 'Take hold of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s robe-corner.' He took hold. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, by supernatural power, rose into the air from that very place, vanished from <s>Rājagṛha</s>, and appeared on the <s>Vaideha</s> mountain. At that time, having seen the fields of the people of <s>Magadha</s>—level, well-laid-out, arranged in rows, beautifully variegated with different planting patterns—he again addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Have you seen these fields, <s>Ānanda</s>—level, well-laid-out, arranged in rows, beautifully variegated with different planting patterns?' 'I have, Venerable Sir.' 'Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, in this manner monks should cut and sew their robes.' The Elder <s>Ānanda</s> informed the monks: 'You should cut and sew your robes in this manner.' The monks began cutting and sewing robes. They made the leaf-shaped patches fall on one side only. body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), wandering through the country of <s>Magadha</s>, reached the forest region. He dwelt in the forest, in the foremost grove. The forest river, due to its proximity, was cool and breezy. In the first watch of the night, the <s>Bhagavān</s> put on the inner robe (<s>antarvāsa</s>). In the middle watch, the upper robe (<s>uttarāsaṅga</s>). In the last watch, he addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Give me the outer robe (<s>saṃghāṭī</s>), <s>Ānanda</s>.' Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having washed his hands, placed the <s>saṃghāṭī</s> upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>. That night was passed by the <s>Bhagavān</s> with the three robes. Then, when dawn had broken, he reflected: 'Whoever in the world are delicate and pleasure-seeking — I am foremost among them. If I am able to manage with three robes, how much more so my disciples.' Having understood this, he addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks): 'Therefore, <s>bhikṣus</s>, monks should possess only the cut three robes (<s>tricīvara</s>).'

They, together with their respective wives, devoted themselves to adornment and did not think about household duties. He said: 'Householder, why are you absorbed in thought?' 'My sons, together with their respective wives, devote themselves to adornment and do not think about household duties. The household will fall into ruin.' He said: 'Why has a marriage not been arranged for <s>Viśākha</s>?' 'Who knows — perhaps he too might become worse.' 'This also cannot be known — perhaps he might become better. If you agree, I shall search for a girl.' 'Do so.' He, while searching, in due course reached <s>Campā</s>.
