children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Since they were stored by <s>Ānanda</s>, a monk should be designated as a counter-custodian of the death-estate in exchange. And this is how the designation should be made: having arranged the seats, having sounded the gong, having summoned the monks by the announcement of the agenda, with the entire <s>Saṅgha</s> seated and assembled, one monk should make a formal motion and then perform the act: "May the noble <s>Saṅgha</s> listen! In this dwelling, the monk <s>Mūlaphalguna</s> has died. His bowl and robes, together with the robe-chest, are in the hands of <s>Ānanda</s>. If it is the proper time and acceptable to the <s>Saṅgha</s>, may the <s>Saṅgha</s> approve this: that the monk <s>Ānanda</s> be designated as counter-custodian of the death-estate of the monk <s>Mūlaphalguna</s>'s bowl and robes together with the robe-chest. This is the formal motion."' The Venerable <s>Upāli</s> asked the Buddha, the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'If, Venerable Sir, a monk dies in one place, his bowl and robes are in another place, and the counter-custodian is in yet another place—to whom do the bowl and robes accrue?' 'To whichever person, <s>Upāli</s>, is the counter-custodian—whether monk or layman.'

body.translated_text: The setting is <s>Śrāvastī</s>. When King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> inaugurated the water-festival, a great assembly of monks, nuns, male lay disciples, and female lay disciples gathered there. At that time, the monk <s>Mūlaphalguna</s> was one to be attended upon by nuns. When the water-festival was at hand, several nuns said to him: 'Venerable one, consider yourself invited. We shall go to the water-festival.' He said: 'But who will look after my bowl and robes?'

body.text: srāvastyāṃ nidānam* / tena khalu samayena navakarmiko bhikṣuḥ kālagataḥ / bhikṣavas tasya pātracīvaraṃ kaukṛtyān na bhājayanti / etat prakaraṇaṃ bhagavata ārocayanti / bhagavān āha / sarvasaṃghaṃ sannipātyāsau lakṣitavyaḥ / kiṃ sambhinnakārī na vā iti / yadi saṃbhinnakārī / sāṃghikaṃ staupikaṃ karoti / staupikaṃ vā sāṃghikam* / (

children.translated_text: [MSV II 146]

children.text: ) evam adhārmikam* / tasya pātracīvaraṃ sacīvaracīvarikaṃ trīn bhāgān kartavyam* / buddhasya / dharmasya / saṃghasya / sāṃghiko bhikṣubhir bhājayitavyaḥ / buddhasantakena buddhapūjā vā gandhakūṭyāṃ stūpe vā navakarma kartavyam* / dharmasantakena buddhavacanaṃ vā lekhayitavyam* / siṃhāsane vā upayoktavyam* / na cet sambhinnakārī sarvam eva bhikṣubhir bhājayitavyam* / nātra kaukṛtyaṃ karaṇīyam* /
children.translated_text: this is unlawful. His bowl and robes, together with the robe-chest, should be divided into three shares: for the Buddha, the Dharma, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>. The <s>Saṅgha</s>'s share should be distributed among the monks. With the Buddha's share, worship of the Buddha should be performed, or repairs and new construction should be done at the fragrance-chamber or <s>stūpa</s>. With the Dharma's share, the Buddha's word should be copied, or a lion-throne should be furnished. If he was not one who mixed funds, everything should simply be distributed among the monks. There should be no remorse in this matter.'

body.translated_text: The setting is <s>Śrāvastī</s>. At that time, a construction-supervisor monk died. The monks, out of scrupulousness, did not distribute his bowl and robes. They reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'The entire <s>Saṅgha</s> should be assembled, and he should be examined: whether he was one who mixed [<s>Saṅgha</s> and <s>stūpa</s>] funds or not. If he was one who mixed funds—[if] he made communal [<s>Saṅgha</s>] property into <s>stūpa</s> property, or <s>stūpa</s> property into communal property—

body.text: śrāvastyāṃ nidānam* / tena khalu samayena saṃbahulā bhikṣavo janapadacārikāṃ caranto 'nupūrveṇa srāvastyām upanagaram anuprāptāḥ* / tanmadhyād eko bhikṣuḥ kālagataḥ / te saṃlakṣayanti / bahir vihārasya bhājayāmaḥ / vihāraṃ praviṣṭānāṃ sabrahmacāriṇo 'pi bhāgaṃ prārthayiṣyantīti / śrāvastī tannivāsibhir gopālakaiḥ paśupālakais tṛṇahārakaiḥ kāṣṭhahārakaiḥ pathājīvair utpathājīvaiś ca manuṣyaiḥ samantād ākīrṇā / te yatra yatra niṣīdanti bhājayāma iti tatra tatra mahājanena parivāryante / te saṃlakṣayanti / vihārasamīpe bhājayāma iti / te vihārasamīpe bhājayitum ārabdhāḥ (

children.text: ) / upadhivārikeṇa dṛṣṭā uktāś ca / āyuṣmantaḥ kiṃ kurutha / tair yathāvṛttaṃ samākhyātam* / sa kathayati / aham api sīmāprāpta iti / tais tasya vivācayato na dattam* / etat prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bhagavata ārocayanti / (
children.translated_text: The requisite-keeper saw them and said: 'Venerable ones, what are you doing?' They told him the events as they had occurred. He said: 'I too have reached the boundary (<s>sīmā</s>).' Despite his protest, they did not give him [a share]. The monks reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
[MSV II 147]

children.text: ) bhagavān āha / antaḥsīmāyām antaḥsīmāsaṃjñino mṛtapariṣkāraṃ bhājayanti / abhājitaṃ durbhājitam* / punar api sīmāprāptaiḥ saha bhājayitavyam* / anyathā sātisārāḥ / evam antaḥsīmāyāṃ vaimatikā bhājayanti / abhājitaṃ durbhājitam* / punar api sīmāprāptaiḥ saha bhājayitavyam* / anyathā sātisārāḥ / bahiḥsīmāyām antaḥsīmāsaṃjñino mṛtapariṣkāraṃ bhājayanti / abhājitaṃ durbhājitam* / punar api sīmāprāptaiḥ saha bhājayitavyam* / anyathā sātisārāḥ / bahiḥsīmāyāṃ vaimatikā bhājayanti / abhājitaṃ durbhājitam* / punar api sīmāprāptaiḥ saha bhājayitavyam* / anyathā sātisārāḥ bhavanti /
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'If those within the boundary, thinking they are within the boundary, distribute the death-estate—improperly distributed, badly distributed. It must be redistributed together with all those who have reached the boundary. Otherwise, there is an offense. Likewise, if those within the boundary who are uncertain [whether they are inside] distribute—improperly distributed, badly distributed. It must be redistributed together with all those who have reached the boundary. Otherwise, there is an offense. If those outside the boundary, thinking they are within the boundary, distribute the death-estate—improperly distributed, badly distributed. It must be redistributed together with all those who have reached the boundary. Otherwise, there is an offense. If those outside the boundary who are uncertain distribute—improperly distributed, badly distributed. It must be redistributed together with all those who have reached the boundary. Otherwise, there is an offense.'

body.translated_text: The setting is <s>Śrāvastī</s>. At that time, many monks traveling on a wandering tour through the countryside arrived by stages at a suburb of <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Among them, one monk died. They thought: 'Let us distribute [his property] outside the monastery. Once we enter the monastery, fellow monks will also claim a share.' <s>Śrāvastī</s> was surrounded on all sides by its resident cowherds, animal keepers, grass-carriers, wood-carriers, and people making their living on and off the roads. Wherever they sat down [thinking] 'Let us distribute,' a great crowd surrounded them. They thought: 'Let us distribute near the monastery.' They began to distribute near the monastery.

body.text: śrāvastyāṃ nidānam* / tena khalu samayena bhikṣuṇā bhikṣor haste

The monks reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Monks, that monk generated trust where no trust was warranted. The robes, which were sent by a monk, were used by him on his own authority—that is, by the trust of the one for whom they were sent.'

children.translated_text: A monk sends robes for another monk. The one for whom they were sent dies. The one who sent them
[MSV II 148]

children.translated_text: uses them by his [the deceased's] trust—improperly used. If, following proper procedure, he designates them as death-estate of the one for whom they were sent—properly designated.

children.translated_text: A monk sends robes for another monk. The one who sent them dies. If, following proper procedure, [the carrier] designates them as death-estate of the one who sent them—improperly designated.

children.translated_text: A monk sends robes for another monk. The one for whom they were sent rejects them. The one who sent them uses them by his [the intended recipient's] trust—
properly used.

children.translated_text: If [the carrier] uses them by the trust of the one for whom they were sent—improperly used.

children.translated_text: A monk sends robes for another monk. The one for whom they were sent dies. If, following proper procedure, [the carrier] designates them as death-estate of the one for whom they were sent—properly designated.
If [the carrier] designates them as death-estate of the one who sent them,
following proper procedure—improperly designated.

children.text: bhikṣur bhikṣoś cīvarakāṇi preṣayati / yasya preṣitāni tena pratikṣiptāni / yena preṣitāni sa ca kālagataḥ / yasya preṣitāni tasya viśvāsena paribhuṃkte / duṣparibhuktāni / yena preṣitāni tasya kalpena mṛtapariṣkārikam adhitiṣṭhati / svadhiṣṭhitāni
children.translated_text: A monk sends robes for another monk. The one for whom they were sent rejects them; the one who sent them also dies. If [the carrier] uses them by the trust of the one for whom they were sent—improperly used. If, following proper procedure, he designates them as death-estate of the one who sent them—properly designated.

children.text: bhikṣur bhikṣoś cīvarakāṇi preṣayati / yasya preṣitāni tena pratikṣiptāni / sa kālagataḥ / yenāpi preṣitāni sa kālagataḥ / yasya preṣitāni tasya kalpena mṛtapariṣkāram adhitiṣṭhati / duradhiṣṭhitāni / yena preṣitāni tasya kalpena mṛtapariṣkārikam adhitiṣṭhati / svadhiṣṭhitāni
children.translated_text: A monk sends robes for another monk. The one for whom they were sent rejects them, and he dies. The one who sent them also dies. If [the carrier] designates them as death-estate of the one for whom they were sent, following proper procedure—improperly designated. If he designates them as death-estate of the one who sent them, following proper procedure—properly designated.

body.translated_text: However, [the rule is]: a monk sends robes for another monk through a [third] monk. If [the carrier] uses them by the trust of the one for whom they were sent—properly used. If he uses them by his own authority rather than [delivering them to] the one who sent them—improperly used.

body.text: // cīvaravastu samāptam* //
body.translated_text: The <s>Cīvaravastu</s> (Chapter on Robes) is completed.
